editorial: If you're looking for a sweet, feel-good animated movie the whole family can enjoy, Ferdinand is a great pick. The story follows a gentle bull who would rather smell flowers than fight, and that simple idea carries the whole film. You meet Ferdinand as a small calf who runs away from a bull-training ranch and ends up living peacefully with a girl named Nina and her dad on a flower farm. Years later, he's huge and strong, but still soft-hearted. When he accidentally causes chaos at a flower festival, he gets sent back to the ranch and chosen for a bullfight in Madrid. The animation is bright and colorful, and the voice cast brings a lot of warmth and humor. The pacing is steady, with plenty of laughs from the supporting animals, especially a trio of hedgehogs and a nervous goat. It's not the deepest animated film out there, but it has heart, a good message about being yourself, and enough action to keep kids entertained. Great for a cozy family movie night. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Ferdinand is sent into the Madrid bullring to face the famous matador El Primero. Instead of fighting, Ferdinand refuses to charge and simply stands his ground, sniffing flowers that Nina tosses into the ring. The crowd, moved by his gentle nature, cheers for him and demands his life be spared. El Primero, unable to bring himself to kill such a peaceful animal, walks away. Ferdinand is freed and returns home to the flower farm with Nina, where he lives happily ever after surrounded by his friends. The twist is that the bull everyone expected to be a fierce fighter turns out to be the gentlest soul in the ring, proving you don't have to be tough to be brave.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves family-friendly animated adventures with heart.
